decision.summary: The Federal Reserve decided to hold the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in June suggests that economic activity expanded at a modest pace during the first half of the year.
changes.explanation: The Fed slightly downgraded its assessment of economic growth during the first half of the year from moderate to modest.

changes.quote: Household spending and business fixed investment advanced, and the housing sector has been strengthening, but mortgage rates have risen somewhat and fiscal policy is restraining economic growth.
changes.explanation: The Committee added a note that rising mortgage rates and government fiscal policy are now acting as headwinds to the recovery.

changes.quote: The Committee recognizes that inflation persistently below its 2 percent objective could pose risks to economic performance, but it anticipates that inflation will move back toward its objective over the medium term.
changes.explanation: A new sentence was added to acknowledge the specific risk that inflation running too low could harm the economy.

tone_quotes.quote: To support a stronger economic recovery and to help ensure that inflation, over time, is at the rate most consistent with its dual mandate, the Committee decided to continue purchasing additional agency mortgage-backed securities at a pace of $40 billion per month and longer-term Treasury securities at a pace of $45 billion per month.

In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee's 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.94% APR costs about $49.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.6% and moved -3 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.37% would fall by about $5.30 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.5%, and employers added an average of 197k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.7% over the past year (June 2013); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.5%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 1.1% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved -2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved 0.18% on the day.

whats_next: The statement signals that the Fed will likely maintain its current pace of asset purchases and low interest rates until labor market conditions improve substantially. According to an educational forecast model, there is an 81% chance the Fed will hold rates at the next meeting.
